program_name: Management of Green Spaces, Forests and Protected Areas
campus: University Campus, Via G. Amendola 165/A, 70126 Bari
academic_requirements: An Italian upper-secondary school diploma or a foreign qualification recognized as equivalent is required.
Admission is open and does not depend on passing a selective entrance examination.
Students take a non-selective initial-knowledge multiple-choice assessment in biology, chemistry, physics and mathematics.
qualification_system_requirements: The foreign school qualification must be recognized as equivalent and must grant university-entry entitlement.

[uncertain] Applicants from schooling systems shorter than 12 years may need supplementary post-secondary study or a foundation course under the central foreign-qualification rules; the precise case-specific rule was not stated on the programme page.
language_requirements: The programme's canonical page and DreamApply record identify Italian as the programme language; no complete English curriculum is offered.

Non-EU applicants residing abroad who enrol in this Italian-taught programme must demonstrate Italian proficiency at B2 or pass the UNIBA Italian-language test, unless covered by a ministerial exemption.
During the degree, students must obtain English-language proficiency at CEFR B1 through an eligibility assessment or recognition of an accepted certificate.
language_level: Italian B2 for applicable non-EU applicants residing abroad; English B1 is an in-programme learning requirement
accepted_language_evidence: Italian B2 or higher certificate issued within the CLIQ quality system
UNIBA Italian-language proficiency test organized by the University Language Centre after Universitaly pre-enrolment
For the curricular English B1 requirement: an eligibility assessment or a certificate from an internationally recognized institute and/or one affiliated with UNIBA
personal_preparation_assessment: A programme-designed, non-selective multiple-choice assessment verifies school-level knowledge in mathematics, biology, physics and chemistry. It contains 10 questions per subject (40 total) and is passed with at least 15 correct answers.
ofa_or_remedial_obligations: A negative result in all or some assessed subjects results in an Additional Educational Obligation (OFA), to be completed during the first year.

Students may use remedial materials on Agripodcast and retake an assessment on that platform; an OFA in biology, chemistry, physics or mathematics is also cleared by passing the corresponding course examination.
Failure to clear the OFA by the second sitting of the autumn examination session prevents the student from taking second-year examinations.
The Interclass Board may exempt holders of an academic qualification, students with foreign-university educational activities, and certain transfer/change-of-programme applicants.
